svg.title: Ultrasound probe types and the image shape each makes
svg.desc: Three probes side by side, each with the shape of image it produces. A linear probe has a flat face and makes a rectangular image the width of the probe; it uses high frequencies for fine detail near the surface, such as vessels, muscles, tendons and the thyroid. A curved (curvilinear) probe has a convex face and makes a wide fan whose top follows the curve of the probe; it uses lower frequencies to see deep into the abdomen and pelvis, including pregnancy scans. A phased array probe has a small flat face and steers its beam electronically to make a fan that starts from a point; its small footprint fits between the ribs for scans of the heart.
